import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import numpy as np

# Read the data
df = pd.read_csv('data.csv')

# Create a figure with multiple subplots
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(16, 12))
gs = fig.add_gridspec(3, 3, hspace=0.3, wspace=0.3)

# 1. Income Distribution
ax1 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 0])
df['Income'].dropna().hist(bins=30, ax=ax1, color='skyblue', edgecolor='black')
ax1.set_xlabel('Income')
ax1.set_ylabel('Frequency')
ax1.set_title('Income Distribution')

# 2. Education Level Distribution
ax2 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 1])
education_counts = df['Education'].value_counts()
ax2.bar(education_counts.index, education_counts.values, color='lightcoral', edgecolor='black')
ax2.set_xlabel('Education')
ax2.set_ylabel('Count')
ax2.set_title('Education Level Distribution')
ax2.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)

# 3. Marital Status Distribution
ax3 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 2])
marital_counts = df['Marital_Status'].value_counts()
colors = plt.cm.Set3(range(len(marital_counts)))
ax3.pie(marital_counts.values, labels=marital_counts.index, autopct='%1.1f%%', colors=colors)
ax3.set_title('Marital Status Distribution')

# 4. Product Categories Spending
ax4 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 0])
product_cols = ['MntWines', 'MntFruits', 'MntMeatProducts', 'MntFishProducts', 'MntSweetProducts', 'MntGoldProds']
product_spending = df[product_cols].sum()
product_names = ['Wines', 'Fruits', 'Meat', 'Fish', 'Sweets', 'Gold']
ax4.bar(product_names, product_spending.values, color='mediumseagreen', edgecolor='black')
ax4.set_xlabel('Product Category')
ax4.set_ylabel('Total Spending')
ax4.set_title('Total Spending by Product Category')
ax4.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)

# 5. Purchase Channels
ax5 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 1])
channel_cols = ['NumWebPurchases', 'NumCatalogPurchases', 'NumStorePurchases']
channel_totals = df[channel_cols].sum()
channel_names = ['Web', 'Catalog', 'Store']
colors_channels = ['#FF9999', '#66B2FF', '#99FF99']
ax5.bar(channel_names, channel_totals.values, color=colors_channels, edgecolor='black')
ax5.set_xlabel('Purchase Channel')
ax5.set_ylabel('Total Purchases')
ax5.set_title('Total Purchases by Channel')

# 6. Age vs Income Scatter
ax6 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 2])
current_year = 2014  # Based on the data dates
df['Age'] = current_year - df['Year_Birth']
scatter = ax6.scatter(df['Age'], df['Income'], c=df['Response'], cmap='coolwarm', alpha=0.6, edgecolors='black', s=50)
ax6.set_xlabel('Age')
ax6.set_ylabel('Income')
ax6.set_title('Age vs Income (Color: Response)')
plt.colorbar(scatter, ax=ax6, label='Response')

# 7. Kids at Home Distribution
ax7 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 0])
df['Total_Kids'] = df['Kidhome'] + df['Teenhome']
kids_counts = df['Total_Kids'].value_counts().sort_index()
ax7.bar(kids_counts.index, kids_counts.values, color='plum', edgecolor='black')
ax7.set_xlabel('Number of Kids at Home')
ax7.set_ylabel('Count')
ax7.set_title('Distribution of Kids at Home')

# 8. Campaign Acceptance Rate
ax8 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 1])
campaign_cols = ['AcceptedCmp1', 'AcceptedCmp2', 'AcceptedCmp3', 'AcceptedCmp4', 'AcceptedCmp5', 'Response']
campaign_acceptance = df[campaign_cols].sum()
campaign_names = ['Cmp1', 'Cmp2', 'Cmp3', 'Cmp4', 'Cmp5', 'Response']
ax8.bar(campaign_names, campaign_acceptance.values, color='orange', edgecolor='black')
ax8.set_xlabel('Campaign')
ax8.set_ylabel('Acceptances')
ax8.set_title('Campaign Acceptance Rates')

# 9. Recency Distribution
ax9 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 2])
ax9.hist(df['Recency'], bins=25, color='lightgreen', edgecolor='black')
ax9.set_xlabel('Recency (days)')
ax9.set_ylabel('Frequency')
ax9.set_title('Customer Recency Distribution')

plt.suptitle('Customer Marketing Data Analysis Dashboard', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', y=0.995)

plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.close()
